Subject: Draft redlines: MSA + Order Form (training & output ownership)

Sean — attaching the MSA and order form with our redlines. Two core asks from EdgeWorks legal: 1) explicit assignment of productized output (they want assignment of output generated by the service when prompts include customer data), and 2) a broad training consent so EdgeWorks can opt their content back into their internal models.

Summary of key redlines attached:
- Section 6 (IP): change "no assignment" language to a grant of "ownership" for outputs created from customer prompts that include proprietary content.
- Section 9 (Feedback / Training): add a clause allowing EdgeWorks to provide feedback and opt-in for retraining; they want a perpetual, royalty-free license back to them.
- Data retention & telemetry: request deletion guarantees and enhanced telemetry export for attribution.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these in whole or propose a working compromise? If we can't grant assignment, they asked for a narrowly scoped productization carveout tied to specific product lines.

Attachments: EdgeWorks_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline), OrderForm_EdgeWorks_20250815.pdf

EdgeWorks Legal

Thanks Priya / EdgeWorks — got the redlines and summary. Appreciate the clarity.

Short answer: we can't accept an assignment of output as written — that would conflict with how we license models and would create downstream productization risks for other customers. That said, we want to get this deal across the finish line and can offer a narrowly scoped compromise:

Proposed compromise (high level):
- Limited productization carveout: EdgeWorks may obtain exclusive assignment for "Customer-Created Outputs" only when (a) output is generated from customer-supplied proprietary data flagged at ingestion, and (b) the output is solely used within a specific EdgeWorks product line described in the order form.
- Training/feedback: allow an opt-in feedback license for retraining that EdgeWorks controls (per-scope, revocable), with an explicit warranty that any models trained with that data will not be re-sold as a general-purpose model without EdgeWorks' permission.
- Telemetry/export: provide scheduled telemetry exports and a contract side-file detailing format and retention.

I copied Marissa (AE) to align on commercial credits/concession budget, and Karthik to advise on legal wording and whether we need to route to Marcus for an exception. Marissa — can you confirm if a carveout like the one above fits within our revenue / concession guardrails?

Thanks —
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Quick legal take and proposed contract language for the carveout.

1) Carveout framing (contract language suggestion):
"Customer-Created Outputs" means outputs generated by Redwood
services where the prompt or input includes Customer Confidential Data and
where Customer has expressly flagged the input as subject to the Productization Carveout in the applicable Order Form. For such Customer-Created Outputs, Redwood grants Customer a limited assignment of title solely for use within the Product Line specified in the Order Form. This assignment does not apply to Redwood's models, training data, or any outputs created from prompts that include public or third-party content.

2) Feedback / training: propose an opt-in, revocable, non-exclusive license from Customer to Redwood to use submitted feedback for internal model improvements, with the following safeguards: feedback is processed only after explicit opt-in, Customer may withdraw consent for future uses, and Redwood will not redistribute resulting general-purpose models derived primarily from Customer Confidential Data without Customer's written consent.

3) Telemetry & export: we will add a schedule for telemetry exports (S3 link/format) and a retention window of 90 days by default; customer may request longer retention at additional cost.

This language should materially close the majority of the risk items. Marcus — because the proposed assignment is an atypical productization concession, please confirm whether we can approve the narrow assignment limited to Product Line + flagged inputs. If not, we'll offer the license-with-exclusive-use covenant instead (narrower than assignment).

If everyone agrees, I can push a tracked-change version to the doc and Marissa can share with EdgeWorks' GC on the call.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
